scope: Page coordinates, graphics state, paths, device colours and Contents arrays checked against the local ISO 32000-2:2020 sponsored EC3 text. The vector API also exercises clause 11 transparency, 8.7 analytic/mesh shadings and shading/tiling patterns, 12.5 annotation appearances and view flags and 10.6 continuous-tone halftone bypass. This is not a conformance certification.

requirements.status: vector pipeline with independent device-colour and state oracles
requirements.gaps: calibrated group blending, subtractive overprint and transfer-region selection
requirements.rule: Page coordinates, initial state, rectangle construction, painting and device colours follow Tables 51, 52, 58 and 59.
Contents-array streams form one lexical sequence with separating whitespace; boundaries may occur between tokens, including within an operation, as specified in Table 31.

requirements.status: conservative default-user-space API; tight geometric bounds remain outside scope
requirements.gaps: Control hulls and stroke/clip envelopes can exceed the smallest painted rectangle; fixed-size annotation views and hairlines use the one-unit reference device.
requirements.rule: 12.3.2.2 defines destination bounds in default user space and clamps them to the crop box. This API shares conservative culling geometry without integer pixel rounding; using control hulls, stroke envelopes and clip envelopes is project policy, not an assertion that their geometric intersections are tight.

requirements.status: opaque Normal fill members elided on Normal RGB scenes without masks, patterns or transfers
requirements.rule: When member opacity is one, its alpha equals its shape and knockout replacement reduces to Normal source-over. Elision retains the original group mask viewport. Exact-area coverage bytes and guarded nearest output rounding are project policy; the composited oracle allows one level under ADR 0004.
requirements.gaps: Non-opaque members, non-Normal scenes, soft masks, transfer functions, patterns and non-RGB blending retain their group surfaces.
